name: watering hole
description: Win by getting one of your animals onto the water hole at d4, the middle square, with none of the animals that eat it beside it; both players move at once. Almost every game is won at the hole, though eating all of the other side's animals wins too. Each round you each choose a move in secret and the two are made together, so every step is a guess about where the other side is going. Two animals stepping onto one square meet, and the one that eats the other wins; a hunter stepping onto the square its prey has just left finds it empty. White's elephants and cats face Black's dogs and rats on a 7x7 board, every animal stepping one square in any direction, and the four kinds form a chain across the two armies: elephant eats dog, dog eats cat, cat eats rat, rat eats elephant. Each of your animals hunts one enemy kind and flees the other, and no meeting is ever two of a kind, so none ends in a tie. Step toward the hole and you may walk into the one animal that eats you; hold back to guard it and the other side may slip through.

provenance.source: docs/archive/plan-simultaneous.md, Q918e: a game designed around simultaneous moves
provenance.history: Q918e (2026-10-15), the showcase of schema 26's rules.simultaneous.tie impossible and the game designed around guessing that docs/archive/plan-simultaneous.md §6.8 asks for: a four-kind food chain split between two armies, so every meeting has a winner, and one shared goal square, so two arrivals in one round are a meeting and not a draw. Drafts v1 to v7 and why each changed are in docs/archive/plan-simultaneous.md, Q918e. Pre-registered there before it was measured. Joined the library from preview by Q934 (2026-10-17): the library's first game played in rounds and its only one with no royal, in which two arrivals on the one shared square are a meeting that always has a winner, so no game is drawn; viable 4-0 at 0.608 on the round roster (Q944a).
